newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Varied debt deals dished out.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Varied debt deals dished out.

text.p: Asian debt markets offered a meagre but varied menu on Wednesday.

In the floating rate certificate of deposit market, a few details emerged on an upcoming US$60 million FRCD for Korea French Banking Corp. Sources said Korea French has verbally mandated five banks to arrange the deal.
They said the facility has a final maturity of five years with a put and a call option in year three.
The issue will be priced at par to float at 50 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
The five mandated arrangers are Fuji International Finance, BFCE Singapore, KDB International Singapore, Bank Austria and Berliner Bank.
Korean French Bank's prior FRCD paid a coupon of 50 basis points over LIBOR and an all-in return of 56 basis points.
In loans, Hong Kong's Hongville Ltd, a unit of Hutchison Whampoa, reportedly is seeking a HK$2.83 billion three-year term loan facility that will be used to re-finance existing debt.
CEF Capital is tipped to be the arranger.

In structured finance, Philippine Airlines Receivables Co Ltd, a special-purpose company of Philippines Airlines, closed a floating rate note issue secured by credit card receivables, arranger Chase Manhattan Asia revealed.
The issue was raised to US$75 million from US$50 million due to oversubscription during syndication.
The amortizing notes have a five-year final maturity and an average life of 2.5 years, bankers said.
The notes were priced at par to float at 230 basis points over the LIBOR. Fees are 50 basis points for senior managers and 25 basis points for managers.
The issue is secured by cash flows generated from U.S. dollar-denominated credit card sales of Philippine Airlines' tickets. It is the first ticket receivables-backed issue in Asia, Chase said.
In global bonds, U.S. agency Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp (Freddie Mac) launched a US$500 million bond. The five-year bonds can be called after two years.
It will be priced during New York trading hours to yield 52 to 53 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.
U.S. Treasuries traded overseas have performed well in the aftermath of U.S. elections, which returned Democratic President Bill Clinton to office while maintaining a Republican dominated Congress.
Looking ahead, Korea Development Bank's US$500 million global bond is expected to be launched very soon, perhaps as early as Thursday.
